comparison_contract: N4-class ROM + HBM3e versus B300 4NP/HBM3e; WSE-3 N5 only as wafer feasibility/physical ceiling anchor

scope: Generated arithmetic identities and loose published/configured ceilings only.
Auxiliary vector/softmax/top-k/Sinkhorn rates are break-even requirements, not configured or measured service ceilings, and are excluded from the utilization maxima.
A passing audit is not evidence for ROM macro timing, simultaneous full-array activity, NoC timing, power delivery, package, yield, or model accuracy.

inputs.contexts_note: the study contexts; a model whose max_context_tokens is lower contributes only the contexts it can serve, so the point matrix is not rectangular
inputs.cost_scope: partial TCO only: assumed acquisition/NRE amortization plus active electricity
inputs.counting_convention: one multiply plus one add equals two operations

interpretation_boundary: Conservative/central/aggressive are deterministic envelopes, not confidence intervals.
No target-node ROM macro, full-wafer read path, package, power, yield, or model throughput has been measured.

A100 is bounded by two explicit deployments: exact offline BF16-resident expansion and a GPU-favorable packed-HBM/on-consumption-BF16 ceiling whose unpack cost is unmeasured and omitted. Neither receives native FP8/MXFP4 execution.
B300 uses official packed checkpoint storage and public low-precision arithmetic roofs; its undisclosed full-FP32 roof is explicitly assumed and swept.

Normalization, nonlinear, softmax-score, top-k, compressor-pool, and Sinkhorn categories are counted and assigned break-even rate requirements, but no vector/top-k service roof or time is assumed; reported token rates remain conditional on those paths fitting the baseline interval.
The auxiliary ledger is not yet operator-complete: activation quantization/scaling, RoPE, residual/hyper-connection elementwise work, dispatch, and other source operations remain under COMP-01.
Same-batch and resident-session-matched comparisons are both emitted because a wafer pipeline has batch times stages resident sessions.

deployment_representations.kv_cache_policy: MEASURED: BF16 main latent (1,024 B) + 256 B index entry, at five contexts from 1,001 to 200,001 tokens. The vendor's own source states the alternative twice (model.py:425 and :532): 'kv could also use fp8 format, though current implementation uses bf16'. The earlier value of this field -- 'FP8 main + BF16 RoPE; FP4 index' -- described the recipe the serving notes suggest, not what the released code does, and the two disagree by 3.2x on the weight-to-KV ratio.
FP8 main + BF16 RoPE; FP4 index

global KV shared across layers: FP4 E2M1 main latent with one E4M3 scale per 16 channels (288 B) plus FP4 index key with one E8M0 scale per 32 (68 B), owned by layers [2, 8, 14, 20]; FP8 sliding-window KV (528 B) per layer, 128 entries, never persisted (SWA Bounded Replay)
